content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, November 11, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Cavity Reduced Bivalent RSV Vaccine Demonstrates Durable Protection in Preclinical Animal Trials by November 8, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Cavity Reduced Bivalent RSV Vaccine Demonstrates Durable Protection in Preclinical Animal Trials Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Respiratory syncytial virus remains a primary viral pathogen responsible for severe lower respiratory tract infections across the globe, presenting an acute clinical burden among infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Epidemiological assessments estimate that the pathogen contributes to approximately thirty-three million lower respiratory tract illness episodes, roughly 3.6 million hospital admissions, and over one hundred thousand pediatric deaths annually in children under five years of age, with ninety-seven percent of these mortalities occurring in low- and middle-income regions. The viral surface fusion glycoprotein mediates host-cell penetration and serves as the dominant target for neutralizing antibodies elicited in human sera. During infection, this fusion protein transitions from a metastable prefusion conformation into an extraordinarily stable postfusion structure, with the most potent neutralizing antibodies selectively recognizing structural epitopes unique to the metastable prefusion architecture. Because these vulnerable antigenic surfaces, notably the apex-localized antigenic site zero, are permanently lost upon irreversible structural rearrangement to the postfusion form, creating molecular strategies to preserve the prefusion state represents a vital objective in structural vaccinology. To overcome the intrinsic conformational fragility of the prefusion glycoprotein without relying on exogenous covalent locks, researchers formulated a structure-guided engineering framework aimed at decreasing internal void spaces within the trimeric viral complex. Utilizing secondary-structure matching superposition to compare the crystallographic templates of the prefusion ectodomain in complex with a neutralizing antibody fragment and the postfusion conformation, the investigators partitioned the resolved protein sequence into seven discrete structural regions. Segments spanning amino acids 26 to 57, 227 to 305, and 306 to 459 demonstrated close alignment between both functional states, whereas segments spanning residues 58 to 72, 73 to 96, 137 to 226, and 460 to 513 exhibited extensive spatial divergence. By prioritizing these conformationally dynamic zones alongside adjacent structural supports such as the apex-neighboring region from residues 227 to 305, the investigators methodically evaluated four distinct molecular stabilization modalities: engineered interprotomer and intraprotomer disulfide bonds, targeted proline substitutions designed to restrict local backbone flexibility at hinge regions, hydrophobic cavity-filling substitutions, and electrostatic charge optimization across the tight protomer packing interface. Initial experimental screening in human embryonic kidney cells systematically interrogated this diverse library of engineered variants to track prefusion expression and structural stability. The platform utilized dual sandwich enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays where binding to the prefusion-specific monoclonal antibody D25 tracked the retention of site zero antigenicity, while binding to motavizumab, which recognizes both prefusion and postfusion states at antigenic site two, monitored total glycoprotein output. Screening encompassed sixteen engineered cysteine pairs, twenty-three single and double proline alterations, one hundred and twenty-six hydrophobic core substitutions across twenty designated cavity sites, and nineteen individual amino acid substitutions replacing aspartic acid at position 486. Among these candidates, the double-proline substitution T267P-N268P and engineered disulfide pairs such as V482C-S502C exhibited robust site zero binding. However, downstream combinatorial analysis showed that adding disulfide linkages to cavity-filling cores offered only marginal stability improvements in purified size-exclusion chromatography homogeneity, whereas designs incorporating dense proline and disulfide mutations imposed substantial non-native mutational burdens on the overall protein scaffold. Discover more Find Vaccines vaccine Vaccine respiratory syncytial virus Respiratory syncytial virus Through systematic combinatorial evaluation and thermal challenge assays conducted at 55 degrees Celsius alongside extended seven-day storage trials at ambient temperature and 4 degrees Celsius, the team identified an optimized five-substitution design designated as RVF-88. This engineered construct completely eschews non-native cysteine bridges, relying instead on four cavity-filling hydrophobic substitutions—N67L, V90Y, S190I, and M289F—paired with a single electrostatic substitution, D486S. At the molecular level, replacing asparagine with leucine at position 67 packs inward toward the alpha-one helical region without perturbing external recognition by antibody D25. Introducing tyrosine at residue 90 within helix alpha-one occupies an internal void to establish hydrophobic contacts with neighboring residues L61, N63, and I292. The S190I substitution inserts a beta-branched isoleucine side chain into a conserved cavity pocket, while phenylalanine at position 289 mediates closer hydrophobic interactions with L93, L96, and F237 adjacent to helix alpha-one. Concurrently, exchanging the acidic aspartate at residue 486 for serine eliminates clustered negative charges within the local acidic triad, alleviating electrostatic repulsion along the interprotomer interface. To support broad antigenic breadth against co-circulating viral lineages, the researchers translated the RVF-88 mutational architecture into constructs representing the circulating subgroups, generating RVF-88A from the subgroup A ON1 lineage and RVF-88B from the subgroup B BA9 lineage. The engineered antigens were adapted for scalable production without purification tags in a clinical-grade Chinese hamster ovary suspension system, where selected monoclonal cell lines demonstrated sustained expression and stable passaging profiles. Biophysical characterization confirmed the structural integrity of both proteins, revealing single or predominant monodisperse peaks by size-exclusion chromatography following repeated freeze-thaw cycles and prolonged ambient storage. Long-term stability assays demonstrated that purified RVF-88A maintained conformational homogeneity after storage at 4 degrees Celsius for six months and at minus 80 degrees Celsius for twelve months, while RVF-88B preserved a predominant monodisperse peak under parallel storage regimes. Differential scanning fluorimetry showed apparent thermal melting temperatures of 60.5 degrees Celsius for RVF-88A and 58.5 degrees Celsius for RVF-88B, demonstrating notable intrinsic thermal stability. Detailed spectroscopic and hydrodynamic analyses verified that the engineered glycoproteins faithfully adopt a trimeric prefusion architecture in solution. Circular dichroism spectroscopy resolved alpha-helical contents of 35.8 percent for RVF-88A and 36.6 percent for RVF-88B, values that closely mirror the prefusion baseline while remaining distinctly lower than the 64.8 percent alpha-helical content measured for the postfusion reference protein. Sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation resolved homogenous species with sedimentation coefficients of 7.72 S for RVF-88A and 7.69 S for RVF-88B at calculated molecular weights of approximately 180 and 182 kilodaltons, cleanly separated from the 7.12 S value characteristic of the postfusion form. Surface plasmon resonance and binding assays revealed sub-nanomolar to low-nanomolar affinities across a broad panel of monoclonal antibodies targeting prefusion neutralizing epitopes, including site zero, site two, site three, site four, site five, and the quaternary prefusion-specific epitope recognized by AM14. Specifically, RVF-88A and RVF-88B bound the apex-specific monoclonal antibody D25 with equilibrium dissociation constants of 0.457 and 0.627 nanomolar, demonstrating quantitative antigenic preservation comparable to established clinical benchmarks. Cryogenic electron microscopy and single-crystal X-ray diffraction experiments verified the atomic mechanism of stabilization and confirmed the intended reduction of the apical hydrophobic cavity. Reconstructions of RVF-88A and RVF-88B bound to the D25 Fab fragment were resolved to 2.96 and 2.77 angstroms, respectively, demonstrating close structural congruence with previously reported prefusion reference coordinates while highlighting subtle localized shifts at the apex. Complementary crystal structures determined from synchrotron diffraction data at 100 Kelvin revealed uncomplexed trimeric prefusion configurations that aligned with the electron microscopy models. Quantitative void calculations of the trimeric prefusion apex demonstrated that RVF-88 constructs possessed substantially lower internal cavity volumes and reduced total cavity surface areas relative to reference prefusion structures evaluated under identical geometric detection thresholds. This marked contraction of apical void space confirms that dense nonpolar side-chain packing across the upper, middle, and basal tiers of the apical helical bundle successfully stabilizes the prefusion head without requiring rigid interprotomer covalent bridges. In vivo immunogenicity was evaluated in female BALB/c mice immunized intramuscularly on days 0 and 21 with an unadjuvanted bivalent formulation containing equal proportions of RVF-88A and RVF-88B at total doses of 2, 5, or 12.5 micrograms, using buffer and five micrograms of commercial ABRYSVO as controls. Two weeks following the secondary immunization, animals receiving five micrograms of RVF-88 exhibited preF-A-specific binding antibody geometric mean titers of 75,155 and preF-B-specific titers of 45,619, exceeding the corresponding titers of 33,635 and 4032 observed in the reference vaccine group. Serum fifty-percent neutralization titers against live RSV A2 reached a geometric mean titer of 246 in the 5-microgram RVF-88 cohort compared to 51 in the ABRYSVO cohort, establishing a statistically significant enhancement at matched dosage. When challenged intranasally with one million plaque-forming units of RSV A2 two weeks post-boost, mice vaccinated with RVF-88 showed minimal weight loss and experienced 4.2- to 5.9-fold reductions in pulmonary viral RNA copies relative to buffer controls, while infectious pulmonary viral titers dropped below the limit of detection in most animals. Protective efficacy and antibody longevity were further substantiated in extended rodent evaluations and challenge models using cotton rats. In durability monitoring of BALB/c mice receiving two doses of five micrograms of RVF-88, antigen-specific binding IgG titers remained elevated through week 22, with neutralizing activity appearing by week nine and persisting through the conclusion of the 154-day observation window. Parallel trials in female cotton rats administered two 24-microgram doses of bivalent RVF-88 demonstrated significantly higher binding antibody titers against both preF-A and preF-B on day 35 compared to dose-matched ABRYSVO controls, alongside numerically higher neutralizing titers against both RSV A2 and RSV B9320 strains. Upon intranasal challenge with either RSV A2 or RSV B9320, RVF-88 vaccination produced significant reductions in both pulmonary viral RNA levels and infectious virus titers relative to buffer controls. In the upper respiratory tract, RVF-88 significantly lowered nasal turbinate viral RNA copies and infectious titers following RSV A2 infection, although neither RVF-88 nor ABRYSVO achieved statistically significant viral reduction in nasal turbinates following challenge with the B9320 strain. Blinded semi-quantitative inflammation scoring revealed comparable or lower tissue disruption scores in RVF-88 groups relative to control cohorts, and enzyme-linked immunospot assays detected measurable interferon-gamma secretion from harvested splenocytes upon stimulation with defined viral fusion peptides. While these preclinical observations highlight the effectiveness of targeted apical cavity reduction for stabilizing viral glycoproteins, the investigators noted key boundaries in interpreting the findings. The enhanced binding titers observed in vaccinated animals may partly reflect homologous antibody capture because RVF-88 antigens served as the plate-coating reagents during enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Additionally, the persistence of viral replication in the nasal passages following subgroup B viral challenge emphasizes that parenteral immunization confers stronger protective effects within deep lung tissue than across upper mucosal barriers. Addressing this mucosal boundary and verifying industrial batch uniformity will define the next phase of clinical development. Advertising Specifications Subscribing Unions Opinions ArchivesMenu Toggle Victories Labor-friendly Businesses Union Giving Politics OutdoorsMenu Toggle Trophy Hunts Outdoor Links EventsMenu Toggle Upcoming Events Golf Tournaments Please Patronize Do Not Patronize $5 For the Fight Subscribe Obituaries UPCOMING ELECTIONS UNION NOTICES Home / Health / RSV: When it’s more than just a cold RSV: When it’s more than just a cold Posted on November 5, 2026 | Views: 202 HAVING RSV may lower immunity and increase the risk of getting COVID-19 for children and adults. And these infections may occur together, which can worsen the severity of COVID-19 illness. For most healthy children, RSV (Respiratory syncytial virus) is like a cold. But some children, especially young infants, get very sick with RSV. So can adults. RSV causes infections of the lungs and respiratory tract. It’s so common that most children have been infected with the virus by age 2. In adults and older, healthy children, RSV symptoms are mild and typically mimic the common cold. Self-care measures are usually all that’s needed to relieve any discomfort. RSV activity in Missouri follows typical seasonal patterns just like the flu, with the respiratory virus season running from fall through spring. Localized viral trends and hospitalizations vary across the state, with metropolitan hubs like St. Louis and Kansas City tracking seasonal respiratory admissions, and some surrounding areas seeing moderate patient volume. According to the latest figures from the Centers for Disease Control, RSV activity is very low in most areas of the country including Missouri and Illinois, but it is increasing. COVID-19 activity remains elevated in some regions, but is declining nationally. Seasonal flu activity is increasing in many parts of the country, but remains low nationally. SIGNS AND SYMPTOMS RSV can cause severe infection in some people, including babies 12 months and younger (infants), especially premature infants, older adults, people with heart and lung disease, or anyone with a weak immune system (immunocompromised). Signs and symptoms most commonly appear about four to six days after exposure to the virus. In adults and older children, RSV usually causes mild cold-like signs and symptoms. These may include: Congested or runny nose. Dry cough. Low-grade fever. Sore throat. Sneezing. Headache. In severe cases, RSV infection can spread to the lower respiratory tract, causing pneumonia or bronchiolitis — inflammation of the small airway passages entering the lungs. Most children and adults recover in one to two weeks, although some might have repeated wheezing. Severe or life-threatening infection requiring a hospital stay may occur in premature infants or in anyone who has chronic heart or lung problems. RSV enters the body through the eyes, nose or mouth. It spreads easily through the air on infected respiratory droplets. You or your child can become infected if someone with RSV coughs or sneezes near you. The virus also passes to others through direct contact, such as shaking hands. The virus can live for hours on hard objects such as countertops, crib rails and toys. Touch your mouth, nose or eyes after touching a contaminated object, and you’re likely to pick up the virus. People at increased risk of severe or sometimes life-threatening RSV infections include adults with heart disease or lung disease and older adults, especially those age 65 and older. RSV vaccines are recommended for all adults ages 75 and older and adults ages 50 – 74 who are at increased risk for severe RSV. There are two immunizations recommended to protect infants from severe RSV: a maternal RSV vaccine (Pfizer’s Abrysvo) given during pregnancy or an infant RSV antibody given to infants after birth. RSV AND COVID-19 Because RSV and coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) are both types of respiratory viruses, some symptoms of RSV and COVID-19 can be similar. In children, COVID-19 often results in mild symptoms such as fever, runny nose and cough. For adults with COVID-19, symptoms may be more severe and may include trouble breathing. Having RSV may lower immunity and increase the risk of getting COVID-19 for kids and adults. And these infections may occur together, which can worsen the severity of COVID-19 illness. If you have symptoms of a respiratory illness, your doctor may recommend testing for COVID-19. Seek immediate medical attention if your child — or anyone at risk of severe RSV infection — has difficulty breathing, a high fever, or a blue color to the skin, particularly on the lips and in the nail beds. Dr. Almira Contractor with WellSpan Pediatrics joined FOX43 Morning News to discuss the risks of these illnesses, symptoms parents should watch for and ways to help keep their families healthy. While the flu may share some symptoms with the common cold, it can lead to more serious complications, including pneumonia, dehydration and hospitalization. Young children and those with certain underlying medical conditions may face a higher risk of severe illness. Advertisement Advertisement Respiratory syncytial virus, commonly known as RSV, is another concern, particularly for infants and young children. The virus can cause breathing difficulties and, in some cases, lead to serious respiratory infections. Contractor also emphasized the importance of flu vaccination, reminding families that it's not too late to get vaccinated, even though flu season has already started. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends annual flu vaccination for everyone 6 months and older, with rare exceptions. In addition to vaccination, parents can help reduce the spread of respiratory illnesses by encouraging frequent handwashing, covering coughs and sneezes, and keeping children home when they're sick. Advertisement Advertisement Parents should also pay attention to symptoms such as difficulty breathing, dehydration or a fever that improves but then returns with worsening symptoms, which may signal a need for medical attention. Watch the video above for more advice from Dr. Contractor on protecting children during flu and RSV season. For more family health information, visit WellSpan Health. content: 沙特阿拉伯儿童呼吸道合胞病毒的流行病学负担、季节性特征与预防策略演变 《Journal of Infection and Public Health》:Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) in Saudi Arabian Children: Epidemiological Burden, Seasonality, and the Evolving Landscape of Prevention 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月06日 来源:Journal of Infection and Public Health 4.8 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是沙特阿拉伯儿童呼吸道疾病的主要病因,尤其在出生后前六个月婴儿中更为突出。沙特研究表明,因呼吸道疾病住院的儿童中RSV检出率约为20–26%,但估计值因人群、场所、诊断方法和研究时段而异。RSV对住院、重症监护入住、机械通气和医疗费用均有显著贡献。病毒传播通常呈季节性,自秋季至早春,12月和1月为高峰,存在地区差异及COVID-19后的变化。RSV-A和RSV-B均有流行,凸显持续分子监测的必要性。预防历来依赖帕利珠单抗(palivizumab)用于特定高危婴儿。新兴策略包括尼塞韦单抗(nirsevimab)和母体融合前F蛋白(prefusion F)疫苗接种,在国际上显示出显著效果,但沙特-specific有效性数据仍不可得。因此,在沙特阿拉伯全国范围内,广泛婴儿预防、强化监测、本地化季节性时间界定、真实世界有效性研究、分子监测及综合经济评估均亟需开展。 研究背景方面,呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是幼儿急性下呼吸道感染(LRTI)的重要病因,疾病负担在婴儿期最为集中。在沙特阿拉伯,RSV一直被认定为住院儿童中的主要呼吸道病原体,但报告检出率因研究人群、地理区域、诊断方法和研究时段而异。多项沙特研究报告约四分之一的儿科呼吸道样本中检出RSV,而在因毛细支气管炎住院的儿童等特定人群中观察到更高比例。理解RSV的局部流行病学、严重程度、季节性和医疗负担对于确定新兴预防策略在沙特阿拉伯的最佳实施方式至关重要。目前存在的问题包括:现有证据多来自单中心、回顾性、医院为基础的研究,缺乏全国代表性的人群数据;分子监测数据在地域和时间上有限;新兴预防策略(如尼塞韦单抗和母体疫苗接种)缺乏沙特-specific的临床有效性或真实世界数据;经济评估依赖国际试验数据输入和假设,而非本地观察数据。因此,开展此项叙述性综述旨在展示和讨论沙特阿拉伯儿童RSV流行病学和疾病负担的现有证据,检查循环的季节和分子模式,并评估已建立和新兴的预防策略,特别关注其在沙特医疗保健背景下的潜在应用。 欢迎下载【ADC药物研发与生产解决方案】,查看各阶段相关工艺流程技术细节! 领 取 研究人员通过两次互补的语义文献检索(使用Elicit平台)开展叙述性综述。第一次检索针对RSV流行病学和季节性,第二次针对预防策略。筛查考虑涉及沙特阿拉伯≤18岁儿童或可提取沙特-specific数据的人群的研究;纳入标准包括RSV作为可单独识别结局、提供发病率/检出比例/住院/死亡/疾病负担/季节性分布的定量信息、实验室确认(PCR、抗原检测、血清学或病毒培养)、适当的观察性/监测/系统综述或荟萃分析设计、样本量至少10例。预防检索考虑评估新兴RSV单克隆抗体、疫苗或其他新型预防方法的人体研究,优先沙特阿拉伯人群、可提取的沙特亚组以及相关中东或海湾合作委员会人群。研究人员手动审查合格出版物并对照原文核实提取信息的准确性、相关性和一致性。由于人群、研究设计、诊断方法和结局定义的差异,发现以叙述方式综合,未进行新的统计汇总。 主要关键技术方法包括:语义文献检索(通过Elicit平台进行两次互补检索)、系统筛查与纳入标准评估、手动数据提取与原文交叉核对、叙述性证据综合。样本队列来源为已发表的沙特阿拉伯及相关国际研究文献,无原始样本采集。 研究结果方面:(1)流行病学负担——患病率与分布:RSV在沙特阿拉伯儿童中被一致认定为主要呼吸道病原体,报告检出比例因临床环境、年龄分布、诊断方法和分母差异而存在显著变化。东部省检出率为26.3%,利雅得研究报告住院或急性病儿童中为22.4%和26.9%。1991至2015年发表的沙特研究综述显示患病率估计范围为0.2%至54%,平均约22.8%。在482例毛细支气管炎队列中,RSV在71/142例受检儿童中检出(50.0%),占病毒阳性儿童的71/132(53.79%)。另一研究中RSV占儿科病毒阳性患者的195/315(61.9%)。较低比例见于更广泛或混合年龄呼吸道人群,包括吉达所有筛查样本的84/834(10.1%)和塔伊夫所有筛查样本的8/5,864(0.14%)。这些差异主要反映研究分母和病例选择的变化,而非确立主要地理差异。(2)年龄与人口学分布:RSV负担主要集中在婴儿和幼儿。中东和北非(MENA)地区系统综述(含沙特数据)显示12个月以下儿童占RSV病例的68.6%。利雅得三级专科医院研究显示77.7%的RSV相关入院发生在出生后前六个月。男性 predominance 也有报告,MENA分析报告59.6%的RSV病例为男性,但年龄似乎是最一致的人口学决定因素。(3)临床严重程度与医疗利用:RSV对儿科住院和重症监护利用有显著贡献。利雅得三级中心队列中,885例RSV阳性儿童中60.3%住院;534例住院患者中26.2%入住重症监护。13.1%的全部病例使用任何类型的通气支持,死亡率为2.4%。吉赞研究中31.8%的RSV阳性患者需要重症监护,40.0%接受氧气或通气支持,死亡率为8.7%。东部省报告平均住院6.5天;利雅得三级中心队列报告中位住院6天、中位重症监护5天。吉赞ICU患者平均住院12.13天,非ICU患者6.24天。(4)严重疾病危险因素:年轻年龄仍是沙特儿童严重RSV疾病最一致的决定因素。早产、慢性肺病(CLD)或支气管肺发育不良(BPD)、先天性心脏病(CHD)及其他显著合并症反复出现在需要住院或预防的儿童中。沙特建模分析显示97%的估计RSV住院发生在不符合帕利珠单抗资格的足月或早产婴儿中。(5)经济负担:国家决策分析模型估计,在典型婴儿队列的第一个RSV季节,RSV将导致约17,179–19,607例住院及超过57,000次急诊就诊,年度医疗负担估计约4.80–6.19亿沙特里亚尔(SAR)。(6)季节性与地理模式——季节性循环:沙特阿拉伯RSV循环呈季节性模式,多数感染发生在较凉爽月份。跨不同时段和区域的研究普遍观察到活动增加从10月至2月或3月,12月和1月最一致地被确定为高峰月份。东部省RSV活动在8月至2月最高,特别是12月和1月;早期利雅得研究记录循环主要在10月至2月,高峰在1月和2月。后续利雅得监测同样显示6–8月RSV活动最低,12–1月最高。吉赞12月占RSV病例最高比例(57/195,29.2%),其次1月(43/195,22.1%)。总体证据支持大致定义为约9月或10月至3月的季节。(7)区域与环境变异:尽管沙特阿拉伯地理和气候多样,现有研究普遍显示凉爽月份RSV predominance,而非明显不同的区域季节。环境条件可能促成这些模式,沙特研究显示RSV检出与温度呈负相关、与相对湿度呈正相关。(8)COVID-19期间及之后的变化:COVID-19大流行显著扰乱了沙特阿拉伯既定的RSV季节性。严格公共卫生措施期间RSV活动显著下降,东部省在大流行期间及随后冬季未检测到RSV感染。RSV循环随后以改变的时间反弹,东部省报告不寻常的2021年8月高峰,利雅得研究也记录到更早的大流行后高峰。这些变化被归因于易感儿童积累,但大流行后改变是否代表沙特RSV季节性的持续变化仍不确定。(9)预防时机启示:RSV活动相对集中在秋冬为沙特阿拉伯季节性预防提供了基础。然而,季节开始和持续时间的变化、常规冬季期外的偶发感染以及近期大流行后转变表明,预防计划应依据当代本地监测而非来自温带国家的固定假设。(10)分子流行病学与RSV多样性:沙特分子研究显示RSV-A和RSV-B均有循环,相对 predominance 随时间变化。利雅得研究报告RSV-A占特征性感染的77%,吉达为64%;利雅得2022–2023季节更近研究显示RSV-B略占优势。基因型分布变化也有记录,早期沙特研究报告RSV-A NA1基因型循环,而吉达和利雅得更近研究确定ON1基因型 predominance,其特征为G蛋白基因72核苷酸重复。RSV-B株主要聚集于BA谱系,特别是BA9,携带G蛋白基因60核苷酸重复。融合(F)蛋白监测重要性突出,利雅得分子研究显示RSV-A分离株F蛋白抗原位点相对高度保守,位点?和II内鉴定出三个氨基酸替换,而位点III、IV和V保持保守;RSV-B分离株抗原有八个替换,包括抗原位点II内六个(含帕利珠单抗结合表位)。这些发现表明沙特阿拉伯循环RSV持续分子进化,支持持续基因组监测。(11)RSV预防——帕利珠单抗:帕利珠单抗是沙特阿拉伯主要RSV免疫预防策略,资格限于严重疾病风险增加的婴儿,特别是早产儿和慢性肺病或血流动力学显著先天性心脏病儿童。利雅得八年队列比较不同给药方案,报告RSV感染率分别为3.9%、5.9%和9.1%,差异无统计学意义。沙特II期研究评估延长七剂方案在18例高危婴儿中的表现,因局部RSV活动可能超过常规五个月季节;方案耐受良好并一般维持目标血清浓度。然而帕利珠单抗作为人群水平预防策略有重要局限,需要每月重复给药且主要保留给高危婴儿,使大多数健康婴儿未受保护。一项沙特毛细支气管炎队列中仅5.6%患者接受过RSV预防。(12)尼塞韦单抗和Clesrovimab:尼塞韦单抗是靶向融合前RSV F蛋白的长效单克隆抗体,设计为单剂后保护整个RSV季节。关键试验和汇总分析显示对医学就诊RSV下呼吸道感染效力约70–80%,对RSV住院62–83%。2025年活系统综述估计对RSV相关住院的真实世界有效性为80.7%(95% CI 76.1–85.2%)。与帕利珠单抗不同,尼塞韦单抗将被动保护扩展到狭义高危群体之外,这与沙特阿拉伯特别相关,因为建模负担主要落在不符合常规帕利珠单抗预防资格的婴儿中。MEDLEY研究中单剂尼塞韦单抗后安慰剂与五剂月度帕利珠单抗在高危婴儿中安全性相似。未鉴定到沙特尼塞韦单抗临床有效性研究。主要沙特-specific证据来自建模:国家决策分析估计90%覆盖率的普遍尼塞韦单抗预防可将RSV相关住院、PICU入住和机械通气减少约58%,急诊和初级保健就诊减少53%,并预防14例年度RSV死亡中的8例,医疗节省SAR 2.74–3.43亿。这些预测依赖国际临床试验效力输入并假设90%覆盖率,而非观察到的沙特尼塞韦单抗有效性或摄取;获取和给药成本未纳入,完整项目实施成本未评估。Clesrovimab是另一种婴儿RSV预防长效单克隆抗体。随机双盲安慰剂对照2b/3期CLEVER试验中,单剂105 mg使医学就诊RSV下呼吸道感染减少60.4%(95% CI 44.1–71.9%),RSV相关住院减少84.2%(95% CI 66.6–92.6%)至150天,严重不良事件频率与安慰剂相似。Clesrovimab终末半衰期较尼塞韦单抗短(44 vs 71天),但两者均提供约五个月保护。其固定105 mg剂量较尼塞韦单抗体重基础给药可能简化交付。未鉴定到沙特-specific有效性数据。(13)母体RSV疫苗接种:母体免疫通过经胎盘转移RSV-specific抗体在生命早期保护婴儿。MATISSE试验中母体二价RSV融合前F(RSVpreF)疫苗接种使出生后前90天严重RSV相关下呼吸道疾病减少81.8%,至180天减少69.4%。苏格兰国家研究随后估计在分娩前14天以上接种疫苗的母亲所生婴儿中,至90天对RSV相关下呼吸道感染住院的有效性为82.2%。现有证据支持母体疫苗接种作为生命最初几个月保护年幼婴儿的有效手段,但与尼塞韦单抗一样,无沙特临床试验或真实世界有效性数据。(14)证据缺口与优先事项:尽管沙特文献不断增长,重要证据缺口仍存。现有研究确立RSV为儿科呼吸道疾病的重要病因,但多数证据源于单中心、回顾性、医院为基础的研究,特别是三级医疗机构。研究人群、诊断方法、病例定义和观察期的差异导致报告患病率和严重程度的广泛变化。全国代表性人群数据仍有限。主要优先事项是发展协调的国家RSV监测,使用标准化定义确定发病率、住院、严重疾病和死亡率。区域监测也需描述沙特阿拉伯各地RSV活动开始、高峰和持续时间差异。分子监测代表另一重要缺口,现有测序数据在地域和时间上有限。最实质性的证据缺口涉及新兴预防策略,沙特经验目前集中于帕利珠单抗,而支持尼塞韦单抗和母体RSV疫苗接种的证据主要来自国际临床试验、真实世界研究和荟萃分析。经济证据也需进一步发展,前瞻性沙特成本效果和预算影响分析纳入实际获取成本、摄取、医疗利用和真实世界有效性将为全国政策决定提供更强基础。实施研究应解决成功摄取的实际决定因素,包括通过产科和儿科服务交付、依从性、父母接受度、医疗提供者意识和各区域公平可及性。 讨论部分总结:现有沙特证据表明RSV是儿科呼吸道疾病的频繁且临床重要病因,最大负担集中在早期婴儿期,住院和重症监护需求显著。这些流行病学特征为评估沙特阿拉伯预防策略的时机和范围提供了基础。RSV活动相对集中在秋冬为季节性预防提供了基础,但季节开始和持续时间的变化、常规冬季期外偶发感染及大流行后转变表明预防计划应依据当代本地监测。分子研究显示RSV-A和RSV-B持续循环和进化,支持在预防日益靶向保守病毒抗原时继续监测。历史上帕利珠单抗用于选定高危婴儿,虽提供了免疫预防既定框架,但资格限制和重复给药需求限制了其人群水平影响。长效单克隆抗体特别是尼塞韦单抗和母体RSVpreF疫苗接种提供了将保护扩展到更广泛婴儿人群的机会,国际证据显示医学就诊RSV疾病和住院显著减少,但直接沙特有效性数据目前缺乏。沙特-specific建模提示普遍尼塞韦单抗预防可显著减少RSV相关住院、PICU入住、机械通气和医疗利用,但更广泛实施决定应得到持续国家监测、本地定义季节性、真实世界有效性和综合经济评估的支持。加强这些证据领域对于制定适合沙特阿拉伯流行病学和医疗背景的RSV预防策略至关重要。 研究结论翻译:RSV在沙特阿拉伯代表显著的儿科呼吸道负担,尤其在早期婴儿期。现有沙特研究一致确定年幼婴儿,特别是六个月以下者,为RSV相关住院和严重疾病最受影响的人群。尽管估计值因环境而异,RSV占儿科呼吸道感染的相当比例并产生显著住院、重症监护利用和医疗支出。在沙特阿拉伯,RSV循环通常呈季节性,秋冬活动增加,高峰发生在12月至1月之间。然而,区域变异、常规季节边界外循环和COVID-19后转变强调需要持续本地监测以指导预防干预时机。分子研究进一步显示RSV-A和RSV-B持续循环和进化,支持在预防日益靶向保守病毒抗原时继续监测。历史上帕利珠单抗用于沙特阿拉伯选定高危婴儿的RSV预防。虽然该方法提供了免疫预防既定框架,但其资格限制和重复给药需求限制了人群水平影响。长效单克隆抗体特别是尼塞韦单抗和母体RSVpreF疫苗接种提供了将保护扩展到显著更广泛婴儿人群的机会。国际证据显示两种方法均大幅减少医学就诊RSV疾病和住院,但直接沙特有效性数据目前缺乏。沙特阿拉伯-specific建模提示普遍尼塞韦单抗预防可显著减少RSV相关住院、PICU入住、机械通气和医疗利用。然而,关于更广泛实施的决定应得到持续国家监测、本地定义季节性、真实世界有效性和综合经济评估的支持。加强这些证据领域对于制定适合沙特阿拉伯流行病学和医疗背景的RSV预防策略至关重要。 研究背景方面,呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是幼儿急性下呼吸道感染(LRTI)的重要病因,疾病负担在婴儿期最为集中。在沙特阿拉伯,RSV一直被认定为住院儿童中的主要呼吸道病原体,但报告检出率因研究人群、地理区域、诊断方法和研究时段而异。多项沙特研究报告约四分之一的儿科呼吸道样本中检出RSV,而在因毛细支气管炎住院的儿童等特定人群中观察到更高比例。理解RSV的局部流行病学、严重程度、季节性和医疗负担对于确定新兴预防策略在沙特阿拉伯的最佳实施方式至关重要。目前存在的问题包括:现有证据多来自单中心、回顾性、医院为基础的研究,缺乏全国代表性的人群数据;分子监测数据在地域和时间上有限;新兴预防策略(如尼塞韦单抗和母体疫苗接种)缺乏沙特-specific的临床有效性或真实世界数据;经济评估依赖国际试验数据输入和假设,而非本地观察数据。因此,开展此项叙述性综述旨在展示和讨论沙特阿拉伯儿童RSV流行病学和疾病负担的现有证据,检查循环的季节和分子模式,并评估已建立和新兴的预防策略,特别关注其在沙特医疗保健背景下的潜在应用。研究人员通过两次互补的语义文献检索(使用Elicit平台)开展叙述性综述。第一次检索针对RSV流行病学和季节性,第二次针对预防策略。筛查考虑涉及沙特阿拉伯≤18岁儿童或可提取沙特-specific数据的人群的研究;纳入标准包括RSV作为可单独识别结局、提供发病率/检出比例/住院/死亡/疾病负担/季节性分布的定量信息、实验室确认(PCR、抗原检测、血清学或病毒培养)、适当的观察性/监测/系统综述或荟萃分析设计、样本量至少10例。预防检索考虑评估新兴RSV单克隆抗体、疫苗或其他新型预防方法的人体研究,优先沙特阿拉伯人群、可提取的沙特亚组以及相关中东或海湾合作委员会人群。研究人员手动审查合格出版物并对照原文核实提取信息的准确性、相关性和一致性。由于人群、研究设计、诊断方法和结局定义的差异,发现以叙述方式综合,未进行新的统计汇总。主要关键技术方法包括:语义文献检索(通过Elicit平台进行两次互补检索)、系统筛查与纳入标准评估、手动数据提取与原文交叉核对、叙述性证据综合。样本队列来源为已发表的沙特阿拉伯及相关国际研究文献,无原始样本采集。研究结果方面:(1)流行病学负担——患病率与分布:RSV在沙特阿拉伯儿童中被一致认定为主要呼吸道病原体,报告检出比例因临床环境、年龄分布、诊断方法和分母差异而存在显著变化。东部省检出率为26.3%,利雅得研究报告住院或急性病儿童中为22.4%和26.9%。1991至2015年发表的沙特研究综述显示患病率估计范围为0.2%至54%,平均约22.8%。在482例毛细支气管炎队列中,RSV在71/142例受检儿童中检出(50.0%),占病毒阳性儿童的71/132(53.79%)。另一研究中RSV占儿科病毒阳性患者的195/315(61.9%)。较低比例见于更广泛或混合年龄呼吸道人群,包括吉达所有筛查样本的84/834(10.1%)和塔伊夫所有筛查样本的8/5,864(0.14%)。这些差异主要反映研究分母和病例选择的变化,而非确立主要地理差异。(2)年龄与人口学分布:RSV负担主要集中在婴儿和幼儿。中东和北非(MENA)地区系统综述(含沙特数据)显示12个月以下儿童占RSV病例的68.6%。利雅得三级专科医院研究显示77.7%的RSV相关入院发生在出生后前六个月。男性 predominance 也有报告,MENA分析报告59.6%的RSV病例为男性,但年龄似乎是最一致的人口学决定因素。(3)临床严重程度与医疗利用:RSV对儿科住院和重症监护利用有显著贡献。利雅得三级中心队列中,885例RSV阳性儿童中60.3%住院;534例住院患者中26.2%入住重症监护。13.1%的全部病例使用任何类型的通气支持,死亡率为2.4%。吉赞研究中31.8%的RSV阳性患者需要重症监护,40.0%接受氧气或通气支持,死亡率为8.7%。东部省报告平均住院6.5天;利雅得三级中心队列报告中位住院6天、中位重症监护5天。吉赞ICU患者平均住院12.13天,非ICU患者6.24天。(4)严重疾病危险因素:年轻年龄仍是沙特儿童严重RSV疾病最一致的决定因素。早产、慢性肺病(CLD)或支气管肺发育不良(BPD)、先天性心脏病(CHD)及其他显著合并症反复出现在需要住院或预防的儿童中。沙特建模分析显示97%的估计RSV住院发生在不符合帕利珠单抗资格的足月或早产婴儿中。(5)经济负担:国家决策分析模型估计,在典型婴儿队列的第一个RSV季节,RSV将导致约17,179–19,607例住院及超过57,000次急诊就诊,年度医疗负担估计约4.80–6.19亿沙特里亚尔(SAR)。(6)季节性与地理模式——季节性循环:沙特阿拉伯RSV循环呈季节性模式,多数感染发生在较凉爽月份。跨不同时段和区域的研究普遍观察到活动增加从10月至2月或3月,12月和1月最一致地被确定为高峰月份。东部省RSV活动在8月至2月最高,特别是12月和1月;早期利雅得研究记录循环主要在10月至2月,高峰在1月和2月。后续利雅得监测同样显示6–8月RSV活动最低,12–1月最高。吉赞12月占RSV病例最高比例(57/195,29.2%),其次1月(43/195,22.1%)。总体证据支持大致定义为约9月或10月至3月的季节。(7)区域与环境变异:尽管沙特阿拉伯地理和气候多样,现有研究普遍显示凉爽月份RSV predominance,而非明显不同的区域季节。环境条件可能促成这些模式,沙特研究显示RSV检出与温度呈负相关、与相对湿度呈正相关。(8)COVID-19期间及之后的变化:COVID-19大流行显著扰乱了沙特阿拉伯既定的RSV季节性。严格公共卫生措施期间RSV活动显著下降,东部省在大流行期间及随后冬季未检测到RSV感染。RSV循环随后以改变的时间反弹,东部省报告不寻常的2021年8月高峰,利雅得研究也记录到更早的大流行后高峰。这些变化被归因于易感儿童积累,但大流行后改变是否代表沙特RSV季节性的持续变化仍不确定。(9)预防时机启示:RSV活动相对集中在秋冬为沙特阿拉伯季节性预防提供了基础。然而,季节开始和持续时间的变化、常规冬季期外的偶发感染以及近期大流行后转变表明,预防计划应依据当代本地监测而非来自温带国家的固定假设。(10)分子流行病学与RSV多样性:沙特分子研究显示RSV-A和RSV-B均有循环,相对 predominance 随时间变化。利雅得研究报告RSV-A占特征性感染的77%,吉达为64%;利雅得2022–2023季节更近研究显示RSV-B略占优势。基因型分布变化也有记录,早期沙特研究报告RSV-A NA1基因型循环,而吉达和利雅得更近研究确定ON1基因型 predominance,其特征为G蛋白基因72核苷酸重复。RSV-B株主要聚集于BA谱系,特别是BA9,携带G蛋白基因60核苷酸重复。融合(F)蛋白监测重要性突出,利雅得分子研究显示RSV-A分离株F蛋白抗原位点相对高度保守,位点?和II内鉴定出三个氨基酸替换,而位点III、IV和V保持保守;RSV-B分离株抗原有八个替换,包括抗原位点II内六个(含帕利珠单抗结合表位)。这些发现表明沙特阿拉伯循环RSV持续分子进化,支持持续基因组监测。(11)RSV预防——帕利珠单抗:帕利珠单抗是沙特阿拉伯主要RSV免疫预防策略,资格限于严重疾病风险增加的婴儿,特别是早产儿和慢性肺病或血流动力学显著先天性心脏病儿童。利雅得八年队列比较不同给药方案,报告RSV感染率分别为3.9%、5.9%和9.1%,差异无统计学意义。沙特II期研究评估延长七剂方案在18例高危婴儿中的表现,因局部RSV活动可能超过常规五个月季节;方案耐受良好并一般维持目标血清浓度。然而帕利珠单抗作为人群水平预防策略有重要局限,需要每月重复给药且主要保留给高危婴儿,使大多数健康婴儿未受保护。一项沙特毛细支气管炎队列中仅5.6%患者接受过RSV预防。(12)尼塞韦单抗和Clesrovimab:尼塞韦单抗是靶向融合前RSV F蛋白的长效单克隆抗体,设计为单剂后保护整个RSV季节。关键试验和汇总分析显示对医学就诊RSV下呼吸道感染效力约70–80%,对RSV住院62–83%。2025年活系统综述估计对RSV相关住院的真实世界有效性为80.7%(95% CI 76.1–85.2%)。与帕利珠单抗不同,尼塞韦单抗将被动保护扩展到狭义高危群体之外,这与沙特阿拉伯特别相关,因为建模负担主要落在不符合常规帕利珠单抗预防资格的婴儿中。MEDLEY研究中单剂尼塞韦单抗后安慰剂与五剂月度帕利珠单抗在高危婴儿中安全性相似。未鉴定到沙特尼塞韦单抗临床有效性研究。主要沙特-specific证据来自建模:国家决策分析估计90%覆盖率的普遍尼塞韦单抗预防可将RSV相关住院、PICU入住和机械通气减少约58%,急诊和初级保健就诊减少53%,并预防14例年度RSV死亡中的8例,医疗节省SAR 2.74–3.43亿。这些预测依赖国际临床试验效力输入并假设90%覆盖率,而非观察到的沙特尼塞韦单抗有效性或摄取;获取和给药成本未纳入,完整项目实施成本未评估。Clesrovimab是另一种婴儿RSV预防长效单克隆抗体。随机双盲安慰剂对照2b/3期CLEVER试验中,单剂105 mg使医学就诊RSV下呼吸道感染减少60.4%(95% CI 44.1–71.9%),RSV相关住院减少84.2%(95% CI 66.6–92.6%)至150天,严重不良事件频率与安慰剂相似。Clesrovimab终末半衰期较尼塞韦单抗短(44 vs 71天),但两者均提供约五个月保护。其固定105 mg剂量较尼塞韦单抗体重基础给药可能简化交付。未鉴定到沙特-specific有效性数据。(13)母体RSV疫苗接种:母体免疫通过经胎盘转移RSV-specific抗体在生命早期保护婴儿。MATISSE试验中母体二价RSV融合前F(RSVpreF)疫苗接种使出生后前90天严重RSV相关下呼吸道疾病减少81.8%,至180天减少69.4%。苏格兰国家研究随后估计在分娩前14天以上接种疫苗的母亲所生婴儿中,至90天对RSV相关下呼吸道感染住院的有效性为82.2%。现有证据支持母体疫苗接种作为生命最初几个月保护年幼婴儿的有效手段,但与尼塞韦单抗一样,无沙特临床试验或真实世界有效性数据。(14)证据缺口与优先事项:尽管沙特文献不断增长,重要证据缺口仍存。现有研究确立RSV为儿科呼吸道疾病的重要病因,但多数证据源于单中心、回顾性、医院为基础的研究,特别是三级医疗机构。研究人群、诊断方法、病例定义和观察期的差异导致报告患病率和严重程度的广泛变化。全国代表性人群数据仍有限。主要优先事项是发展协调的国家RSV监测,使用标准化定义确定发病率、住院、严重疾病和死亡率。区域监测也需描述沙特阿拉伯各地RSV活动开始、高峰和持续时间差异。分子监测代表另一重要缺口,现有测序数据在地域和时间上有限。最实质性的证据缺口涉及新兴预防策略,沙特经验目前集中于帕利珠单抗,而支持尼塞韦单抗和母体RSV疫苗接种的证据主要来自国际临床试验、真实世界研究和荟萃分析。经济证据也需进一步发展,前瞻性沙特成本效果和预算影响分析纳入实际获取成本、摄取、医疗利用和真实世界有效性将为全国政策决定提供更强基础。实施研究应解决成功摄取的实际决定因素,包括通过产科和儿科服务交付、依从性、父母接受度、医疗提供者意识和各区域公平可及性。讨论部分总结:现有沙特证据表明RSV是儿科呼吸道疾病的频繁且临床重要病因,最大负担集中在早期婴儿期,住院和重症监护需求显著。这些流行病学特征为评估沙特阿拉伯预防策略的时机和范围提供了基础。RSV活动相对集中在秋冬为季节性预防提供了基础,但季节开始和持续时间的变化、常规冬季期外偶发感染及大流行后转变表明预防计划应依据当代本地监测。分子研究显示RSV-A和RSV-B持续循环和进化,支持在预防日益靶向保守病毒抗原时继续监测。历史上帕利珠单抗用于选定高危婴儿,虽提供了免疫预防既定框架,但资格限制和重复给药需求限制了其人群水平影响。长效单克隆抗体特别是尼塞韦单抗和母体RSVpreF疫苗接种提供了将保护扩展到更广泛婴儿人群的机会,国际证据显示医学就诊RSV疾病和住院显著减少,但直接沙特有效性数据目前缺乏。沙特-specific建模提示普遍尼塞韦单抗预防可显著减少RSV相关住院、PICU入住、机械通气和医疗利用,但更广泛实施决定应得到持续国家监测、本地定义季节性、真实世界有效性和综合经济评估的支持。加强这些证据领域对于制定适合沙特阿拉伯流行病学和医疗背景的RSV预防策略至关重要。研究结论翻译:RSV在沙特阿拉伯代表显著的儿科呼吸道负担,尤其在早期婴儿期。现有沙特研究一致确定年幼婴儿,特别是六个月以下者,为RSV相关住院和严重疾病最受影响的人群。尽管估计值因环境而异,RSV占儿科呼吸道感染的相当比例并产生显著住院、重症监护利用和医疗支出。在沙特阿拉伯,RSV循环通常呈季节性,秋冬活动增加,高峰发生在12月至1月之间。然而,区域变异、常规季节边界外循环和COVID-19后转变强调需要持续本地监测以指导预防干预时机。分子研究进一步显示RSV-A和RSV-B持续循环和进化,支持在预防日益靶向保守病毒抗原时继续监测。历史上帕利珠单抗用于沙特阿拉伯选定高危婴儿的RSV预防。虽然该方法提供了免疫预防既定框架,但其资格限制和重复给药需求限制了人群水平影响。长效单克隆抗体特别是尼塞韦单抗和母体RSVpreF疫苗接种提供了将保护扩展到显著更广泛婴儿人群的机会。国际证据显示两种方法均大幅减少医学就诊RSV疾病和住院,但直接沙特有效性数据目前缺乏。沙特阿拉伯-specific建模提示普遍尼塞韦单抗预防可显著减少RSV相关住院、PICU入住、机械通气和医疗利用。然而,关于更广泛实施的决定应得到持续国家监测、本地定义季节性、真实世界有效性和综合经济评估的支持。加强这些证据领域对于制定适合沙特阿拉伯流行病学和医疗背景的RSV预防策略至关重要。 content: Advertisement Subscribe now Log in November 11, 2026 07:29 E-Paper E-Magazine Corporate CEO Talk Biz Link PR Newswire Media OutReach Newswire Investing M&A Outbound Investment Investing in Haiphong Your Consultant KPMG PwC Indochine Counsel Vilasia Ansarada Green Growth Energy Efficiency Rethinking Plastics BASF Property Green Buildings Industrial Properties Money Insurance Smart Payment Trends Stock Monitor Infographics Timeout Travel Hotels & Restaurants The Insider Entertainment Lifestyle Sports Photos Society Swing for the Kids CSR World News Society Swing for the Kids CSR 79 per cent of people with chronic conditions say respiratory viruses disrupt daily life: survey November 05, 2026 | 17:25 (0) user say Share Email Print GSK has announced new survey findings, highlighting the substantial and often prolonged disruption that respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, can cause to the daily lives of adults with chronic health conditions. RSV may affect the health of people with chronic conditions and their ability to maintain daily activities. Photo: GSK These kinds of disruptions can negatively impact mental health, reduce confidence in managing existing conditions, and lead to increased dependence on others to manage daily tasks. To mark respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) awareness week (November 2-8), a global survey, commissioned and funded by GSK, of 6,041 adults aged 18 and over across 10 countries, explored RSV awareness and experiences among people living with certain chronic health conditions. RSV Awareness Week 2026 is designed to increase understanding of RSV and its impact on adults and people living with certain chronic health conditions. The campaign encourages adults who may be at increased risk to recognise RSV as more than a seasonal respiratory virus by highlighting the disruption it can cause to health, independence and everyday life, and by inspiring more proactive, informed conversations with healthcare professionals. These conditions include cardiovascular disease, diabetes, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), chronic kidney disease, and hypertension. The impact of respiratory viruses on those surveyed was particularly pronounced for some groups. 52 per cent of adults with asthma said their symptoms worsened when they experienced a respiratory virus, along with 45 per cent of those with COPD, 35 per cent of those with chronic kidney disease, 29 per cent of those with cardiovascular disease, and 27 per cent of those with diabetes. Across all respondents, more than a third (36 per cent) experienced a longer recovery than expected, one quarter (25 per cent) needed additional general practitioner or primary care visits, and 18 per cent visited urgent care. Among those who had experienced RSV specifically, the effects could last well beyond the initial infection. 40 per cent said their health was disrupted for a month or more, while nearly 1 in 10 (9 per cent) said it took over a year for their health to return to normal or that they had still not fully recovered. More than half (55 per cent) described their RSV symptoms as moderately severe or very severe, rising to 68 per cent among respondents with chronic kidney disease or COPD, 64 per cent among those with cardiovascular disease, and 63 per cent among those with asthma. Dr. Elena DeAngelis, country medical director of GSK Vietnam, said, “For people living with chronic conditions, managing their health is an everyday priority. Contracting RSV or another respiratory infection can have impacts beyond a few days of feeling unwell, affecting their ability to care for themselves and continue the activities that are meaningful to them. People with chronic conditions should speak with healthcare professionals about ways to help protect themselves against RSV.” RSV is an increasingly recognised cause of respiratory illness among older adults aged 60 and over. In 2019 in developed countries alone, RSV was estimated to account for around 470,000 hospitalisations and 33,000 in-hospital deaths in adults aged 60 and over. Adults living with cardiovascular disease, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, asthma, and COPD are at increased risk of severe RSV disease such as lower respiratory tract disease and its complications. In Vietnam, based on modelled estimates over a five-year period, approximately 4.6 million RSV-associated acute respiratory infection cases are projected to occur among adults aged 60 years and older. These estimates include approximately 200,000 hospitalisations and nearly 18,000 deaths attributable to RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease. Despite this potential impact, awareness doesn’t always translate into conversations with healthcare professionals. Four in five respondents said they were concerned that a respiratory virus could interfere with management of their chronic condition or worsen their symptoms. Yet almost half (46 per cent) had not discussed RSV with a healthcare professional within the past two years, including one third (33 per cent) who said they had never discussed it. This gap was particularly notable among older respondents: 66 per cent of adults aged 18–49 had discussed RSV with a healthcare professional within the past two years, compared with 45 per cent of adults aged 50 and over. These findings highlight an important gap between the potential impact of RSV and how seriously that risk is being considered by people living with certain chronic health conditions. Greater awareness of RSV and its potential consequences can help encourage patients to pay more attention to this virus when speaking with healthcare professionals. These survey findings underline the need to make RSV a more visible part of respiratory health and chronic condition discussion. For adults who may be at increased risk, speaking to a healthcare professional can help them better understand RSV and the steps they can take to help prevent an RSV infection. Proactive disease prevention and personalised treatment: a new approach in the era of population ageing At the 2026 conference “Research and Application in Medicine,” organised by the Vietnam Medical Association on August 28, experts shared updates on scientific research and clinical practice in disease prevention and treatment, ranging from life-course immunisation to advanced treatment solutions for non-communicable diseases. Symposium highlights RSV risks in older adults Population ageing underscores the urgent need for proactive prevention to protect older adults, particularly those with underlying conditions, from the serious health risks associated with Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). GSK supports medical community in raising awareness of severe asthma in Vietnam Leading experts in respiratory medicine and allergy-immunology gathered at the scientific symposium in Ho Chi Minh City on September 27 to share insights into the pathophysiology of severe asthma, the role of type 2 inflammation and current approaches to disease management. Researchers found that patients infected with respiratory syncytial virus had greater odds of severe acute respiratory infection when compared to those infected with influenza virus, showing an adjusted odds ratio of 7.88 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 5.4 to 11.51. The odds of severe disease were also significantly higher for respiratory syncytial virus when compared to human adenovirus with an adjusted odds ratio of 3.21 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 2.14 to 4.81, human metapneumovirus with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.76 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.24 to 2.50, human parainfluenza virus with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.63 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.14 to 2.33, and human rhinovirus with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.52 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.13 to 2.04. The investigation addressed acute respiratory infections, particularly severe acute respiratory infections, which the authors noted impose a huge disease burden globally while population-based data in China remain limited, especially regarding incidence and hospitalization estimates. Conducted between October 2023 and April 2025, the research integrated multi-source data across Chongqing, encompassing national hospital-based surveillance of 12,669 outpatients presenting with influenza-like illness and 3,694 inpatients diagnosed with severe acute respiratory infection, totaling 16,363 respiratory infection patients. This clinical dataset was combined with electronic medical records from the local health system as well as official census records. To derive population-level metrics, the authors implemented a multi-component surveillance and modeling strategy. They conducted a pilot survey that weighted pathogen detection rates using established case definitions for influenza-like illness, severe acute respiratory infection, and acute respiratory infection. In addition, they carried out a community-based healthcare utilization survey designed to weight the proportion of individuals seeking healthcare. Using these weighted inputs, the team applied a modified multiplier model to estimate population-based incidence and hospitalization rates for acute respiratory infections associated with six specific respiratory viruses, alongside analyses of seasonality and age-specific epidemiological patterns. Discover more Study Biology Check Symptoms infections Track Outbreaks Donate to Research Epidemiological trends revealed distinct age distributions across the six monitored viruses. The detection rate of influenza virus peaked among adolescents and adults, whereas respiratory syncytial virus and human metapneumovirus primarily affected infants and the elderly. In contrast, human adenovirus, human rhinovirus, and human parainfluenza virus were most prevalent among preschool-aged children. These variations in pathogen prevalence across demographic groups corresponded with sharp differences in the overall burden of disease across different life stages. Using the modified multiplier model, researchers estimated that incidence and hospitalization rates per 100,000 person-years were highest in children under 5 years old across all evaluated pathogens. In this youngest age bracket, human rhinovirus accounted for an incidence rate of 30,183 and a hospitalization rate of 2,153 per 100,000 person-years, human metapneumovirus recorded an incidence of 22,774 and hospitalization of 514, respiratory syncytial virus showed an incidence of 22,181 and hospitalization of 2,065, influenza virus reached an incidence of 13,086 and hospitalization of 807, human parainfluenza virus had an incidence of 7,824 and hospitalization of 556, and human adenovirus registered an incidence of 6,991 and hospitalization of 1,487. Hospitalization rates per 100,000 person-years also rose among individuals aged 60 years and older, led by human rhinovirus at 170, respiratory syncytial virus at 80, influenza virus at 70, human metapneumovirus at 54, human adenovirus at 27, and human parainfluenza virus at 23. The authors concluded that distinct age distributions and the high odds of severe acute respiratory infection risk from specific viruses such as respiratory syncytial virus support targeted prevention, and that integrating multi-source surveillance with sentinel surveys can yield population-level, real-world estimates of respiratory virus disease burden. content_title: Health officials see sharp increase of flu and RSV cases in children
content: TEXAS — Chances are, you know someone who is sick or recovering from an illness. Health officials say there’s been a sharp increase in influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) cases in children. Within the state of Texas, there’s been an increase in flu cases, particularly influenza A, according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data and local health officials. The Texas Department of State Health Services started reporting flu cases at the beginning of October, and according to its Respiratory Illness Interactive Dashboard , flu and RSV cases are still high. Texas hospitals and urgent care centers are seeing more children who have the flu every day, but Dr. Natalie Tarrant from Texas Children’s Hospital said we haven’t even seen the peak of flu season yet. “Definitely started earlier than you asked last year. And we don’t know if that means that flu season will just be shifted, where the whole thing starts earlier and ends earlier, or if that means that it’s just going to be a worse year than last year. Last year was worse than the average year for flu,” Tarrant said. But when should you take your child to see a doctor? Dr. Suzanne Whitworth from Cook Children’s Hospital said that, when it comes to children, you have to trust your gut. “Any time you have anxiety and your radar goes off, that you need to see a doctor, call. Either call one or go to urgent care. For sure, you want to go see a doctor if there is any difficulty breathing,” Whitworth said. Dr. Whitworth said a fever can also indicate if your child is very ill. “For healthy, normal children, fever is anything that's a 100.4 or higher rectally. And so if your child has significant fever and they’re not acting right and not feeling okay or dehydrated or not feeling well, that’s another reason to give your doctor a call,” she said. According to Dr. Tarrant, the best way to protect your children from the flu is prevention, and she recommends parents get their children the flu shot. “Vaccination is key. It’s it’s really exciting... as a pediatrician, a new vaccine comes out that changes the landscape of what we see in the office,” Tarrant said. “And the RSV vaccine has been amazing for us. Flu vaccine, we always recommend universally for everybody, but especially the babies, because the babies have a lot of trouble with flu.”

content_title: Children’s Mercy Kansas City Will Keep Kids Under 13 Off Its Inpatient Units Starting Nov. 10 as RSV and Flu Season Builds
content: Sun, November 8, 2026 at 8:30 PM UTC Tuesday, Nov. 10, is the day the youngest visitors lose their place at the bedside at Children’s Mercy Kansas City. From that date, children 12 and under, which means every child under 13, will not be allowed on the hospital’s inpatient units, a rule the hospital says is tied to respiratory virus season, which includes RSV, flu and COVID-19. The rule was announced in an Oct. 22 post on the hospital’s Parent-ish blog by pediatric infectious disease physicians Dr. Edward R. Lyon and Dr. Christelle M. Ilboudo. The hospital’s visitor pages, updated Nov. 6, spell out who is affected and who is not. Who Can and Cannot Come Up to the Inpatient Floors According to the hospital’s visitor guidelines , children 12 and under “will not be able to visit patients in the hospital” once the viral season rules begin. Visitors ages 13 to 16 may come, but they must always be with an adult. All visitors must feel well and be free of illness. Parents and guardians are treated differently. The hospital’s visiting hours page says they are part of the care team rather than visitors, and they may be with their child around the clock. They receive a green wristband, must sign in and have to follow all safety precautions. Up to two parents, guardians or authorized adults may stay overnight in the patient’s room. Other guests may visit from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. Visitors 16 and older need a driver’s license or other photo ID and must wear the sticker they are given. The page notes that exceptions are sometimes possible and tells families to ask their child’s nurse. The restrictions do not apply to clinic or outpatient visits. A family whose child is admitted after a clinic or emergency room visit does face a practical problem, though. According to the hospital, brothers and sisters 12 and under who came along cannot go up to the inpatient unit, so families are told to plan for another caregiver for those children. Why the Cutoff Falls at Age 12 Children’s Mercy says the reasoning is about both risk and habits. The hospital’s visiting hours page states that children 12 and under are the most likely to catch these viruses and the least likely to follow the habits that stop them from spreading. The Parent-ish post puts it more briefly: children 12 and under are the most at risk of catching a virus. Ilboudo is quoted on the visitor guidelines page making the broader point: “Anyone who has a respiratory virus can give it to someone else.” The hospital says the rules protect sick children, their families and staff. The post describes how the viruses move. RSV spreads through respiratory droplets or when a person touches a contaminated surface and then touches the face. Influenza also travels in droplets and, the doctors write, can last at least a week and can be deadly, so it should not be dismissed as “not that bad.” The hospital’s visitor pages add that the policy can change during periods of high infection risk. The timing lines up with the calendar. The CDC says on its RSV page that RSV spreads in fall and winter and usually peaks in December and January. What the CDC and Children’s Mercy Say About RSV and Flu in Young Children The Children’s Mercy doctors write that RSV is the leading cause of infant hospitalization in the U.S., and that most hospitalized infants had no chronic medical problems. The American Academy of Pediatrics makes a similar point on its RSV campaign page , calling RSV the most common cause of hospitalization in children under age 1. For most healthy children RSV looks like a cold. The Parent-ish post says it usually clears in one to two weeks but can cause bronchiolitis and pneumonia in infants under 6 months and in children with weakened immune systems. The CDC’s page on RSV symptoms says very young infants may show only irritability, decreased activity and breathing difficulties. Symptoms usually appear four to six days after infection and tend to develop in stages. The CDC advises calling a health care professional if a child has difficulty breathing, is not drinking enough fluids or is getting worse, and it says aspirin should not be given to children. Flu carries its own numbers. The CDC’s page on flu in children estimates 6,000 to 25,000 flu-related hospitalizations a year among children under 5. Annual vaccination is recommended for everyone 6 months and older, and children 6 months through 8 years need two doses if it is their first vaccination, if they have had only one previous dose or if their history is unknown. The second dose comes at least four weeks after the first. The Children’s Mercy doctors say not to delay the flu shot while waiting for a particular type. For babies, the post lists two one-time antibody injections that are not vaccines: nirsevimab (Beyfortus) for infants entering their first RSV season, and clesrovimab (Enflonsia) for infants under 1. It also names Abrysvo, an RSV vaccine given during pregnancy so mothers pass antibodies to the baby. Parents are told to ask their child’s doctor about eligibility. An earlier Parent Diaries report on RSV in babies under 6 months covers how symptoms tend to progress. The CDC’s list of flu emergency warning signs for children includes fast or difficult breathing, bluish lips or face, ribs pulling inward with each breath, dehydration, a child who is not alert, seizures and a fever above 104 degrees that does not respond to medicine. It also lists any fever in a child younger than 12 weeks. Get stories like this by email. Sign up for The Parent Diaries Letter . The investigation, published as a brief research report in Frontiers in Public Health, evaluated 438 participants and identified fourteen positive individuals, yielding an estimated prevalence with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning from 1.8 to 5.3 percent. Respiratory viruses remain a primary global public health concern and represent leading causes of acute respiratory infections worldwide. University students represent a potentially important group for viral circulation because of frequent social interaction. Evidence regarding respiratory virus circulation in university populations from Latin America remains limited. Discover more Healthcare Tour Colleges infections To evaluate viral prevalence and examine the proportion of infections among individuals without symptoms, researchers gathered a convenience sample of healthcare students between January 4 and February 3, 2026. The multicenter study was conducted among healthcare university students from universities located in Quito, Guayaquil, and Cuenca, Ecuador. Discover more Study Biology Check Symptoms View Census Data Get Health Tips Diagnostic evaluations were conducted on site by collecting nasopharyngeal samples and analyzing them with a combo rapid antigen point-of-care test designed to detect respiratory syncytial virus, Influenza A, Influenza B, and Adenovirus. In parallel with antigen testing, investigators systematically recorded sociodemographic and epidemiological variables. Among the fourteen students who tested positive for at least one respiratory pathogen, Influenza A virus and respiratory syncytial virus were the most frequently observed single detections, each identified in four participants. Adenovirus was confirmed as a single detection in three participants, and the authors documented three cases of viral coinfection within the positive group. Clinical symptom tracking revealed that eight of the fourteen positive participants, representing 57.1 percent, were asymptomatic at testing, while six participants, or 42.9 percent, reported experiencing respiratory symptoms. The analysis revealed a statistically significant association between the presence of respiratory symptoms and viral detection, with an observed significance level of p less than 0.001. The authors observed that because more than half of the infected students exhibited no symptoms, respiratory viruses may circulate unnoticed within university settings. The study concluded that overall respiratory virus detection was low in this cohort and demonstrated that rapid antigen tests are operationally feasible point-of-care tools for on-site screening in academic environments. content_title: Medical Societies Back New Respiratory Vaccine Guidance
content: RESPIRATORY vaccine guidance has gained unified support from four leading medical societies ahead of the 2026–2027 virus season. The American Thoracic Society (ATS), American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology (AAAAI), American College of Chest Physicians (CHEST), and Society of Critical Care Medicine (SCCM) have unanimously endorsed recommendations for influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 vaccination in adults and children. The joint endorsement aims to provide consistent, evidence-based recommendations for clinicians managing patients with respiratory conditions, particularly those vulnerable to severe viral illness. The multisociety Vaccine Guidance Review Panel was established following changes to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) processes in 2025. According to the participating organizations, these changes resulted in potentially harmful modifications to vaccination schedules, raising concerns about consistency with established scientific evidence. In response, the panel reviewed and endorsed the vaccine recommendation development processes and resulting guidance from four medical organizations: the American Academy of Pediatrics, American Academy of Family Physicians, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Infectious Diseases Society of America. The panel also reached consensus on guidance aligned with ACIP recommendations issued before June 2025, reinforcing a coordinated approach to respiratory disease prevention. The endorsement covers influenza, RSV, and COVID-19 vaccination recommendations across pediatric and adult populations. A particular priority is ensuring that clinicians caring for patients with chronic or acute respiratory diseases have access to consistent vaccination guidance as seasonal respiratory virus circulation increases. The organizations emphasized that preventive vaccination remains an essential component of protecting patients against severe respiratory illness. Michelle Ng Gong, ATS President, highlighted the importance of clear recommendations for clinicians treating patients with serious lung disease, particularly during periods of uncertainty surrounding national vaccination policies. For physicians, the endorsement establishes a unified professional position on respiratory vaccination and provides a framework for discussing preventive care with patients. The participating societies emphasized that consistent recommendations can strengthen clinical decision-making, support patient education, and promote equitable access to preventive healthcare. The collaboration also reinforces the importance of integrating vaccination into routine respiratory and critical care, particularly for populations at greatest risk of severe illness. By aligning recommendations across specialties, the panel aims to reduce confusion and strengthen confidence in evidence-based vaccination ahead of the respiratory virus season. Reference American College of Chest Physicians (CHEST). Multisociety Panel Endorses Vaccine Recommendations to Protect Respiratory Health. November 5, 2026. Among the fourteen students who tested positive for at least one respiratory pathogen, Influenza A virus and respiratory syncytial virus were the most frequently observed single detections, each identified in four participants. Adenovirus was confirmed as a single detection in three participants, and the authors documented three cases of viral coinfection within the positive group. Clinical symptom tracking revealed that eight of the fourteen positive participants, representing 57.1 percent, were asymptomatic at testing, while six participants, or 42.9 percent, reported experiencing respiratory symptoms. The analysis revealed a statistically significant association between the presence of respiratory symptoms and viral detection, with an observed significance level of p less than 0.001. The authors observed that because more than half of the infected students exhibited no symptoms, respiratory viruses may circulate unnoticed within university settings. The study concluded that overall respiratory virus detection was low in this cohort and demonstrated that rapid antigen tests are operationally feasible point-of-care tools for on-site screening in academic environments. content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, November 11, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology AAPR ratio shows modest link to bacterial type in pediatric RSV by November 10, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 AAPR ratio shows modest link to bacterial type in pediatric RSV Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A retrospective study published in BMC Microbiology has identified a potential association between the Albumin-to-Alkaline Phosphatase Ratio, known as AAPR, and the specific type of bacterial co-infection in children suffering from respiratory syncytial virus, or RSV. The study focused on 153 children with laboratory-confirmed RSV who also had bacterial co-infections, aiming to evaluate the discriminative performance of AAPR and explore relevant biological pathways. RSV infection in children is frequently complicated by bacterial co-infection, a condition that significantly aggravates clinical outcomes. The AAPR has recently emerged as a novel marker in this field, prompting the researchers to investigate its utility. The primary objective was to determine the association between AAPR levels and the phenotypes of Gram-positive versus Gram-negative bacterial co-infection. By analyzing this specific cohort, the study sought to provide insights into the underlying biological mechanisms that might link these metabolic markers to infection types. The study employed a retrospective design, analyzing data from 153 pediatric patients. To determine the independent association and dose-response relationship between AAPR and infection phenotypes, the researchers utilized multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses. Diagnostic performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, or AUC. Additionally, an exploratory systems biology analysis was performed to identify candidate genes and signaling pathways potentially relevant to the observed association. Discover more Engineering job board Research publication platform Scientific instrument sales Laboratory equipment supplier Biotech startup funding The multivariable logistic regression results demonstrated that elevated AAPR was independently and inversely associated with the likelihood of Gram-positive infection. Specifically, the odds ratio was 0.37, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.15 to 0.89 for the highest versus the lowest tertile. This suggests that children with higher AAPR values were less likely to have Gram-positive bacterial co-infections compared to those with lower values. The restricted cubic spline analysis showed no evidence of a nonlinear association, with a P value for non-linearity of 0.456. The association remained similar after nonlinear adjustment for age and was directionally consistent across age strata. However, the relationship was attenuated after normalization using age-specific pediatric alkaline phosphatase reference limits. This indicates that while the association is present, its strength may be influenced by age-related variations in alkaline phosphatase levels. The researchers noted that the inverse association with Gram-positive infection was a key finding, highlighting the potential role of AAPR in differentiating bacterial types. In terms of diagnostic performance, AAPR alone showed modest discriminative performance, with an AUC of 0.599. When AAPR was added to other standard markers such as C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, and neutrophil count, the AUC increased from 0.455 to 0.613. However, this improvement did not reach the conventional threshold for statistical significance, with a P value of 0.051. This suggests that while AAPR may add some value to existing diagnostic panels, it is not yet a standalone tool for distinguishing between bacterial co-infection types. The exploratory systems biology analysis identified several inflammation-related pathways as candidates for further investigation. These included the interleukin-17, tumor necrosis factor, and other pathways involved in immune responses. The identification of these pathways provides a potential biological basis for the observed association between AAPR and bacterial co-infection phenotypes. Further research is needed to confirm these pathways and understand their specific roles in the context of RSV and bacterial co-infections. Discover more Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Donate to Research Find Study Aids The study has several limitations that should be considered when interpreting the results. The retrospective design and the relatively small sample size of 153 patients may limit the generalizability of the findings. The modest discriminative performance of AAPR alone and the lack of statistical significance when added to other markers indicate that more research is needed to validate its clinical utility. Despite these limitations, the study provides valuable insights into the potential role of AAPR as an immuno-metabolic marker in pediatric RSV infections. The inverse association with Gram-positive bacterial co-infection and the identification of relevant inflammation pathways offer promising avenues for future research. content: Skip to main content Main navigation Top stories Health Crime Politics Business Tech Culture Sports Weird 1-1-2 Top stories Health Crime Politics Business Tech Culture Sports Weird 1-1-2 Image Cropped view of doctor in latex gloves holding syringe and vaccine on blurred foreground near patient - Credit: IgorVetushko / DepositPhotos - License: DepositPhotos Health RSV vaccination Ikazia Hospital Rotterdam COPD Zorginstituut Nederland covid-19 pandemic » More tags « Less tags Share this article: Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Elderly people also vulnerable to RS virus; Doctors call for vaccinations Friday, 6 November 2026 - 21:10 The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), commonly associated with serious infections in babies and young children, also poses a significant health risk to older people, particularly those with chronic lung and heart conditions, Dutch lung specialists have said to NOS. They are calling for vulnerable elderly people to receive RSV vaccinations to prevent serious illness and hospital admissions. However, there is a disagreement over who should pay for the vaccines. The Dutch healthcare reimbursement authority, Zorginstituut Nederland, has not yet recommended including them in the basic health insurance package. It expects to issue a new assessment in early 2027. RSV is a common winter virus, and infections among older people can have serious consequences, including pneumonia, hospitalisation and death. One of the doctors featured in the report is Chantal Kroesse, a pulmonologist at Ikazia Hospital in Rotterdam. “We know better now. During the Covid-19 pandemic, a rapid test became available that allowed us to test for influenza, Covid-19 and RSV simultaneously. That was when we immediately began to see the impact of the virus." Kroesse has been pushing for better protection for patients with chronic lung conditions. The pulmonologist managed to convince a health insurer to reimburse RSV vaccinations for vulnerable patients. This quickly led to the number of RSV hospital admissions among the relevant patient group falling from 95 to 34, a reduction of 64 percent. She argues that vaccinating vulnerable patients is also worthwhile because the costs of hospital admissions are considerably higher than those of vaccination. "One vaccination can help prevent a serious infection and hospital admission. Do the maths. A vaccine costs around 200 euros, while a hospital admission can easily cost thousands." RSV stands for respiratory syncytial virus. It is a highly contagious virus that causes infections of the respiratory tract. It is particularly well known in the Netherlands because almost all children contract it before their second birthday. In babies, it can cause serious respiratory problems, including bronchiolitis and pneumonia. The Dutch National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM) specifically identifies older people, people with heart or lung conditions, and those with weakened immune systems as groups at increased risk. A study published last week identified 97,279 hospital admissions for acute respiratory infections among 63,420 patients aged 50 and older. The estimated annual rate of RSV-related respiratory infection admissions was 0.70 per 1,000 people among those aged 50 and older. Among people aged 75 and older, that figure increased to 1.92 per 1,000. During peak months, RSV accounted for up to 30 percent of hospital admissions for acute respiratory infections, with patients staying in hospital for an average of seven to eight days. "An RSV infection can become much more than just a few days of having a cold for someone with COPD,” Kroesse said. "The infection can put such a strain on the lungs that someone needs additional oxygen or has to be admitted to hospital."
